subject: Startups
title: Amazon's Bookstore Gambit
description: A short lesson to help you apply Amazon's Bookstore Gambit.

hook.text: Jeff Bezos quit a cushy Wall Street job in 1994 to sell books online from his garage in Bellevue, Washington.

buildup.text: He chose books because they were easy to ship and had millions of titles no single store could stock.

discovery.text: Amazon went public in 1997 at $18 a share. Bezos told investors to expect years of losses. Most stayed anyway.

twist.text: Books were just the wedge. Bezos always planned to sell everything. The bookstore was a Trojan horse.

climax.text: Amazon became the 'everything store' and later a cloud giant with AWS. The bookstore strategy worked perfectly.

punchline.text: He sold books to build a company that sells everything.

quiz.question: Why did Bezos initially choose to sell books online?
options: Books were easy to ship with huge catalog potential
Books had the highest profit margins
